source.paper: McDonnell, Huang, Cui, Hewak, Smith 2018, 'Probing Excitons, Trions and Dark Excitons in Monolayer WS2 using Resonance Raman Spectroscopy', Nano Lett. 18, 1428, doi:10.1021/acs.nanolett.7b05184 (author manuscript in the dataset record)

items.text: The Raman intensity (A1' in particular) increases strongly on cooling, by roughly an order of magnitude at 4 K relative to 295 K
items.locator: text after Fig. 1: 'As the temperature decreases the Raman intensity increases significantly, by approximately a factor of ten at 4K'

items.text: The excitation energy of maximum enhancement moves to higher energy on cooling (room-temperature resonance a single peak near 2.02 eV; at 4 K higher and structured), following the exciton energy that decreases with increasing temperature
items.locator: Fig. 2 text: 'at room temperature the resonance has the form of a single peak centered at 2.02eV ... the central energy of the resonance increases'; Fig. 5b

items.text: At low temperature the resonance develops structure (exciton plus trion channels, incoming and outgoing resonances), whereas at room temperature it is one broad peak
The trion contribution weakens much faster with temperature than the exciton one (trion-trion amplitude down about 22 times from 4 K to 295 K, exciton-exciton about 40 percent)
Comparing temperatures at one fixed laser wavelength mixes the intensity change with the shift of the resonance; a proper comparison needs the full excitation profile at each temperature
items.locator: Fig. 2 (resonance center moves with temperature); follows from the resonance-profile method of the paper

items.text: Thin-film interference on SiO2/Si and its temperature dependence should be corrected (paper: micro-reflectivity at each temperature); these spectra are not interference corrected
items.locator: Methods; dataset readme ('corrections for REF not applied')

items.text: Asks how the actual sample temperature / absence of laser heating was verified (e.g. Stokes/anti-Stokes ratio)
items.locator: Methods: 'absence of laser induced sample heating was further confirmed using measurements of the Stokes/Anti-Stokes ratio'

wrong_claims.text: Attributes the order-of-magnitude intensity increase on cooling to the Bose-Einstein (n+1) factor (which changes the Stokes intensity of a 417 cm-1 mode by only about 15 percent between 295 K and 4 K)
Claims the resonance moves to lower excitation energy on cooling

notes: Twelve spectra: 4, 150, 295 K, each at the dataset excitation energies closest to 2.11, 2.07, 2.03 and 1.99 eV. The factor of ten is the paper's value for interference-corrected profiles; in these uncorrected data the peak A1' height is also about ten times larger at 4 K than at 295 K. The Bose factor in w1 is a textbook Stokes population factor (Cardona, Light Scattering in Solids I, 1983).
